title: The Utility of Scots Cognates and Germanic Roots in English Etymological Pedagogy
author: Yang Cheng-han (楊承翰)
summary: Exploring comparative lexicography and early Scots cognates to accelerate English vocabulary acquisition.
content: For autodidactic language learners and educators, unlocking English vocabulary through its historical Germanic roots—particularly through early Scots cognates—provides an intuitive architectural framework for retention and comparative analysis.

title: Unpacking Hesed (חֶסֶד): Covenantal Faithfulness Across Translations
author: Research Wing
summary: A deep exegesis of the Hebrew root Hesed, mapping its occurrences across the Old Testament and Greek Septuagint.
content: In Hebrew lexicography, few words capture the depth of God's covenant relationship with humanity as intensely as Hesed (חֶסֶד - Strong's H2617). Often translated as 'lovingkindness' or 'steadfast love'.
